Now I understand the issue. The problem is in `src/defu.ts`. When the `defaults` object has `__proto__` as an own property, `Object.assign({}, defaults)` pollutes `Object.prototype` because `Object.assign` uses `[[Set]]` semantics, and setting `__proto__` on a regular object updates its prototype instead of creating a regular property.

The fix is to use `Object.create(null)` instead of `{}` to create the target object for `Object.assign`, since objects created with `Object.create(null)` have no prototype, so `__proto__` is treated as a regular property key.

When `defaults` has `__proto__` as an own property, `Object.assign` uses `[[Set]]` semantics. Setting `__proto__` on a regular object updates its prototype rather than creating a regular property. This is because `__proto__` is a special accessor property defined on `Object.prototype` that changes the object's prototype.

`Object.create(null)` creates an object with no prototype (i.e., `null` prototype). Since there's no prototype chain, there's no `__proto__` accessor property to intercept the assignment. So when `Object.assign` tries to set `__proto__`, it simply creates a regular own property on the object, treating it as a normal key.

This fix ensures that `__proto__` in the defaults is treated as a regular property key, preventing prototype pollution attacks.
